ます-form stem かい (kai) + たいです (tai desu). The 〜たい ending conjugates like an い-adjective.
Negative of かいたいです (“want to buy”): たい → たくないです (takunai desu).

items.note: Attaches to a noun: noun + の まえに (no mae ni), e.g. かいぎの まえに ("before the meeting"). For a verb instead, use the dictionary form + まえに (mae ni).
items.reviewNote: Written 〜の まえに in the source.

items.note: Dictionary-form verb + まえに (mae ni) = "before doing ..."; たべる (taberu) is the plain form of たべます (tabemasu).
ます-form stem いき (iki) + たいです (tai desu). Conjugates like an い-adjective.
Negative of いきたいです ("want to go"): たい → たくないです (taku nai desu).
Past of いきたいです ("want to go"): たい → たかったです (takatta desu).

items.note: With 〜たい (tai) the object may take が (ga) instead of を (o); ワインを のみたいです is equally correct.

items.english: (I) want to eat some good sushi.
items.target: おいしいおすしをたべたいです
items.note: 〜たい (tai) states only the speaker's own wish, never someone else's.

items.english: Smith-san will send the materials before the meeting.
items.target: スミスさんはかいぎのまえにしりょうをおくります
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa kaigi no mae ni shiryō o okurimasu
items.note: Pattern: person は + noun + の まえに (no mae ni) + verb — the action happens before that event.

items.english: Smith-san does stretching exercises every day before going to bed.
items.target: スミスさんはまいにちねるまえにストレッチをします
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa mainichi neru mae ni sutorecchi o shimasu
items.note: Pattern: dictionary-form verb + まえに (mae ni) + main verb. ねる (neru) is the plain form of ねます (nemasu, "go to bed").

items.english: What kind of place do you want to live in in the future?
items.target: しょうらいどんなところにすみたいですか
items.pronunciation: shōrai donna tokoro ni sumitai desu ka
items.note: Asking about a future hope with 〜たいですか is acceptable even to someone of higher status; for everyday wishes it can sound too direct.

items.english: I want to live near the sea.
items.target: うみのちかくにすみたいです
items.pronunciation: umi no chikaku ni sumitai desu
items.scene: answering what kind of place you want to live in one day

items.english: I want to study Japanese. Is there a good school near here?
items.target: にほんごをべんきょうしたいです。このちかくにいいがっこうがありますか
items.pronunciation: nihongo o benkyō shitai desu. kono chikaku ni ii gakkō ga arimasu ka

items.english: There is a party from 7:00 p.m.
items.target: ごご７じからパーティーがあります
items.ttsText: ごごしちじからパーティーがあります
items.pronunciation: gogo shichi-ji kara pātī ga arimasu
items.note: 〜から (kara) here marks a start time. あります (arimasu) is used for events as well as objects.

items.english: I'll buy wine before the party.
items.target: パーティーのまえにワインをかいます
items.pronunciation: pātī no mae ni wain o kaimasu
items.note: noun + の まえに (no mae ni) + verb = "before (the event), do ..."
Nearly homophonous with びょういん (byōin, "hospital"); this salon word has a long "yō."

items.english: Smith-san started studying Japanese before coming to Japan.
items.target: スミスさんはにほんにくるまえににほんごのべんきょうをはじめました
items.pronunciation: Sumisu-san wa nihon ni kuru mae ni nihongo no benkyō o hajimemashita
items.note: くる (kuru) is the plain form of きます (kimasu, "come"). Dictionary form + まえに (mae ni) is the same whether the main verb is present or past (here はじめました, "started").

items.note: Japanese speakers usually part with a phrase naming the next meeting rather than さようなら (sayōnara): じゃ、また + a day or time, e.g. じゃ、また すいようびに ('see you Wednesday'). Contrast またこんど (mata kondo) from Lesson 16, which defers vaguely to 'some other time' instead of naming one.
